# https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/overview

Source: https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/overview

In SurrealQL, clauses can be used to alter the way a query is executed. They are used in the following ways: 
  * •
[`EXPLAIN`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/explain): Explain the query plan.
  * •
[`FETCH`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/fetch): Fetch all the fields of related records.
  * •
[`FROM`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/from): Specify the table(s) or other target(s) to query from.
  * •
[`GROUP`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/group-by): Group the results by a set of fields.
  * •
[`LIMIT`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/limit): Limit the number of results.
  * •
[`OMIT`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/omit): Omit related records.
  * •
[`ORDER`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/order-by): Specify the sort order of the results.
  * •
[`SPLIT`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/split): Split the results into a set of subqueries.
  * •
[`START`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/start): Return the results of a query starting from a certain point.
  * •
[`WHERE`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/where): Specify a condition that acts as a filter.
  * •
[`WITH`](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/clauses/with): Replace the default table iterator with an index iterator.
